h: Make a Proper Evening of It
p: Victoria works brilliantly as a meeting point because half of London seems to pass through it. Trains, the Tube and the coach station are all within a few minutes' walk, so friends coming in from Surrey, Sussex or the other side of the city can all land in the same place without a long trek. That's half the battle with any group night out sorted before a dart has been thrown.

If darts isn't something you've done since a holiday camp years ago, a couple of simple pointers help. Stand side-on to the board with your front foot near the line, keep your elbow fairly still and let your forearm do the work, then follow through towards where you want the dart to go. Don't worry about technique too much though. The games are built so that a lucky arrow can turn things on its head, and that's half the fun.

Allow a good couple of hours if you're planning to eat and drink as well as play, and get there a little before your booked slot so you're not eating into your time at the oche. Smart-casual is the vibe, nothing fancy needed.

For a fuller day, Tate Britain is a pleasant walk away along Millbank, and the Apollo Victoria and Victoria Palace theatres sit right by the station if you fancy a show first. Westminster and the river are close enough to stroll to afterwards for the lights on the water.
